# Viewer models

Paths for model inputs below are relative to this directory. Generated figures and
screenshots are stored at repository-root `artifacts/model_review/<robot>/`;
script paths and commands are relative to the repository root.

| Model | Source revision | License |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Go2 | [unitreerobotics/unitree_ros @ 3ae893d](https://github.com/unitreerobotics/unitree_ros/tree/3ae893d905d11795ddf1075825ee5010364a1109/robots/go2_description) | BSD-3-Clause |
| Aibo ERS-7 | [dkotfis/aibo_ros @ eec7a9d](https://github.com/dkotfis/aibo_ros/tree/eec7a9dc21779a289eb3bfa48d66cedd830176d3/aibo_description) | MIT |

Go2 `robot.urdf` follows upstream. Aibo's joint axes, offsets and four foot frames follow [Tekkotsu ERS-7.kin @ 6b7ea9a](https://github.com/touretzkyds/Tekkotsu/blob/6b7ea9afb76feb115eaa375a3c0e07d8473a432a/project/ms/config/ERS-7.kin). The numeric reference is in `aibo_ers7/kinematics_reference.json`; lengths convert mm to m, +X-forward becomes +Y-forward, and the base is translated +0.162 m in Z to retain the mesh coordinate convention. Body-aligned link frames preserve Tekkotsu's joint axes and FK. Neck tilt/pan share a pivot, with nod 80 mm above; leg rotor-to-elevator offsets are 62.5 mm. Foot frames now have explicit knee-to-foot offsets. The 17 original joint angular ranges are restored from the pre-edit imported URDF, recorded in `aibo_ers7/original_limits.json`; `headPan` retains the source magnitude ±1.5882 rad with the reversed endpoints put in ascending order. Added mouth/ear limits retain their Tekkotsu values. Source soft-controller metadata remains omitted; this viewer enforces the explicit hard limits.

The original Aibo meshes retain their approximate zero-pose placement through visual/collision frame rebasing; paw meshes are centered on the reference foot frames. These meshes are not dimensionally calibrated to Tekkotsu. Invalid or missing revolute limits fail on load. `mesh_bounds.json` contains local-space mesh bounds derived from upstream STL vertices or Collada scene-transformed vertices, before URDF mesh scale and visual origin. The viewer draws linkage and optional mesh bounding boxes; original Go2/Aibo source meshes are now bundled for offline audit/rendering; the interactive viewer does not load their triangles. Missing bounds fail explicitly.

Aibo adds `mouth` (-55°..0°), `earL` and `earR` (0°..10° each) to the source's 17 joints, using Tekkotsu's named actuators. Unnamed ear mesh frames are fixed transforms. New parts use 5 mm joint-marker spheres, not anatomical meshes; no independent meshes or measured inertias are supplied. Their explicit zero mass, effort and velocity are kinematic-only placeholders, not hardware ratings; their torque margins are N/A. The viewer animates their angular ranges kinematically, including continuous interpolation between ear endpoints. Its source contains placeholder masses and a redundant second base visual origin; the viewer uses the first origin, consistent with common URDF loaders. Aibo's +Y forward is rotated to the viewer's +X for display. Imported mass/COM are URDF values, not calibrated hardware measurements.

Material overlay uses relative density (1× = original URDF link masses); all link masses scale together. Torque uses the same Stage 1 descendant point-mass inertia estimate at 10 rad/s², excluding gravity/contact and link rotational inertia. Margin uses URDF `effort`; continuous torque is unavailable. Aibo effort values are upstream placeholders.

## Pupper v3

Imported from [G-Levine/pupper_v3_description @ 1a3c859](https://github.com/G-Levine/pupper_v3_description/tree/1a3c8590189d3a406219d155f4177afc491a7d77), MIT license retained in `pupper_v3/LICENSE`. Source is `description/urdf/pupper_v3.edited.fixed.urdf`; original STL meshes are bundled. `source.json` records provenance and adaptations. Joint transforms, limits, inertias and mesh scales are preserved. Mesh paths are relative; the MuJoCo compiler tag and empty world/floating joint are removed because the viewer controls root pose. Four massless fixed foot frames use upstream collision sphere centers. Negative mesh scales are correctly mirrored when computing viewer bounds.

12 actuated joints; imported link mass totals 3.170 kg (model value, not a measured hardware mass). Startup uses upstream zero joint pose. URDF effort limits are simulation metadata, not a verified motor torque envelope.

Run `uv run python -m src.components.pygame_mass_viewer --model pupper`; key `4` selects Pupper alongside keys `1/2/3`. The existing viewer shows linkage and mesh bounds. `artifacts/model_review/pupper_v3/pupper_v3.png` shows full STL geometry in two views; regenerate with `uv run --with trimesh python -m src.components.model_tools.pupper_v3.render`.

### Pupper joint-axis audit and linkage correction

`pupper_v3/axis_audit.json` records circle fits to the original STL planar mounting faces (37 mm diameter, 48 convex-hull perimeter vertices per selected face). Reproduce with `uv run --with trimesh --with scipy python -m src.components.model_tools.pupper_v3.audit_axes`. Facet normals supply axis directions; circle fits supply interface centers. Incoming URDF axis orientation selects among matching circular interfaces; residuals are reported rather than assumed zero. This is a mesh/URDF consistency check, not metrology of hardware.

Right-front joint 1 interface center is approximately (75, -48.9, 0) mm in the body frame, joint 2 is (64.1501, -83.5000, 0) mm. Their separation is 36.2613 mm, even though their two perpendicular axis lines intersect at the common URDF frame origin (75, -83.5, 0) mm. For these first two joints on all legs, perpendicular axis residual is below 0.001 mm. Knee-axis residual is approximately 0.050 mm; source rounding is a possible cause, not a verified explanation.

The viewer uses separate physical interface positions with the original filled torque-color dots and gray linkage lines. Decorative interface rings and gold axis lines were removed at user request; the original camera fit and help-panel layout are restored. Connecting lines join measured interfaces, replacing the merged 2-DOF marker and body-center spokes. Display centers are projected onto unchanged URDF axes (maximum correction about 0.05 mm); FK, IK, inertias and torque calculations still use the original kinematic frames. These straight connectors depict rigid-link connectivity, not the exact bent shape of the material. Pupper retains the original default automatic joint motion and random reach, as do the other imported models. B and R toggle these modes; `--no-babble --no-stage3-reach` requests a static comparison. Switching models does not disable random reach. `axis_comparison.png` compares meshes and corrected linkage under the same camera and pose.


### Go2 / Aibo display-axis audit

`src/components/model_tools/audit_display_axes.py` reproduces `go2/display_axis_audit.json` and `aibo_ers7/display_axis_audit.json` from the exact upstream mesh revisions above. `mesh_sources.json` records each source URL and SHA-256; the audit checks every mesh it uses. Run:

```sh
uv run --with trimesh --with scipy --with pycollada python -m src.components.model_tools.audit_display_axes
uv run --with trimesh --with scipy --with pycollada python -m src.components.model_tools.render_axis_review
```

Go2 already has twelve distinct movable reference origins. Its hip-to-thigh axis-origin offset remains 95.5 mm, and thigh-to-calf offset remains 213 mm. Circle fits locate the hip mounting lip at local X approximately ±61.316 mm and the selected thigh face at local Y approximately ±48.495 mm. The fitted radii are 28.5 and 47.75 mm, with circle residuals below 0.001 mm. Their centers miss the URDF axes by 0.665–0.694 mm; the marker is explicitly projected onto the original axis. This discrepancy is recorded and **does not justify changing the kinematic axes**. The chosen face is a display landmark, not a motor center of mass. No reliable circular knee mounting face was identified by this method; all four knee markers explicitly retain their URDF reference origins. Degenerate planar facets are excluded before convex-hull fitting; there is no random-jitter repair.

Aibo's left/right front shoulder origins coincide at (0, 65, 162) mm; the rear pair coincides at (0, -65, 162) mm. Each shoulder marker now lies where its original axis exits the coarse body STL toward its own leg. Root-frame X coordinates are RF +46.0476, LF -46.3195, RB +45.8915, LB -46.1388 mm. These are **shell landmarks, not measured motor centers**. Source STL geometry is too coarse and uncalibrated to independently establish hardware shaft positions. The left/right shoulder groups separate; the documented shared neck/pan and tail pivots remain (20 DOFs, 18 display locations). Other Aibo joints explicitly retain their URDF reference markers.

The runtime requires a complete audit, verifies its URDF/provenance hashes, and rejects missing, stale, unknown-method or off-axis anchors. Zero reference offsets are an explicit audited choice, not a missing-data fallback. The interactive viewer keeps its original dot styles, torque colors, gray connector styling, camera, panels, default animation and current angular ranges. All transforms, axes, limits and inertias in both URDFs remain unchanged by this display audit. Marker offsets affect only drawing; randomized FK, IK, torque, COM and animation comparisons against the unanchored model are covered by regression tests.

`artifacts/model_review/go2/axis_comparison.png` and `artifacts/model_review/aibo_ers7/axis_comparison.png` compare complete source meshes, old linkage and corrected linkage in the same pose/camera. These light-background diagnostic figures use uniform dot colors for legibility; the actual interactive palette remains unchanged. `viewer_before.png` / `viewer_after.png` in each `artifacts/model_review/<robot>/` directory are full actual viewer screenshots at the same static startup pose. In the diagnostic plots, straight gray connectors describe connectivity, not exact material profiles.


Go2 connectivity correction: drawing every URDF joint produced false bones to rotor inertias, sensors and `calflower` collision helper frames, plus crossing body-center spokes. `UrdfModel.go2_linkage_edges()` now supplies the same explicit topology to pygame and the comparison renderer: four perimeter edges through FL–FR–RR–RL hip mounts, plus hip–thigh–calf–foot for each leg (16 total segments). Auxiliary frames remain in FK, inertia and collision metadata but are excluded from the visible skeleton. The middle comparison panel intentionally preserves the faulty previous frame-tree drawing; the right panel shows the corrected topology. Projection can still overlap front/back limbs; no cross-leg limb edges or torso diagonals exist in the new topology. Original dot colors, line styling, animation and limits are unchanged.


Aibo connectivity correction: its leg chains already had the correct joint order, but drawing the entire frame tree added four body-center spokes and two `earR_frame` / `earL_frame` coordinate stubs. The explicit skeleton now uses the RF–LF–LB–RB shoulder perimeter, each shoulder–elevator–knee–paw chain, front/rear perimeter midpoints to neck/tail, and the existing neck/head/face and tail joint chains. Midpoints are display connectors, not extra joints or measured bones. Fixed paw endpoints remain; ear helper frames remain in FK but are not drawn as material. Shared neck/pan and tail pivots remain coincident. Both pygame and the right comparison panel use `skeleton_segments()`; the middle panel retains the old frame-tree drawing. No angular limits, FK, animation controls or marker styling changed.
